Design an alternative investigation into lying using a field experiment of children in a school
and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying lying in practical and methodological terms.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by the ‘individual explanation of behaviour’ in psychology?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one finding from the Milgram study that supports the individual explanation of
behaviour.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of investigating the individual and situational
explanations of behaviour using the Milgram study as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the Milgram study has applications to everyday life. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question in this section.

text: Milgram conducted a study to investigate obedience.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘validity’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Haney, Banks and Zimbardo (prison simulation)
Tajfel (intergroup categorisation)
Bandura et al. (aggression)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What problems may psychologists have when they attempt to make their studies valid?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘psychometric test’. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)
Billington et al. (empathising and systemising)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the quantitative data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What are the weaknesses of using psychometric tests in psychology?
